name: Partial Atrioventricular Septal Defect with Ventricular Hypoplasia
aliases: Partial AV Septal Defect with Ventricular Underdevelopment
Partial Atrioventricular Canal Defect with Hypoplastic Ventricle

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Partial AV Septal Defect with Ventricular Hypoplasia

criteria.description: Presence of a partial atrioventricular septal defect characterized by an ostium primum atrial septal defect and cleft mitral valve
Hypoplasia of one ventricle confirmed by imaging showing reduced ventricular chamber size and wall thickness
Abnormalities of the atrioventricular valves including cleft mitral valve or abnormal tricuspid valve morphology
Signs of congestive heart failure or cyanosis in neonate or infant

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a partial atrioventricular septal defect with documented ventricular hypoplasia on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical presentation.

searchTerms: heart septum defect near lower atrium

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cleft mitral valve causing mitral regurgitation
pathognomonic.notes: Common valve abnormality associated with partial AVSD
searchTerms: mitral valve leak from split leaflet

common.notes: Manifested by tachypnea and poor feeding

common.symptomName: Cyanosis on exertion or at rest
common.notes: Resulting from right-to-left shunting or ventricular dysfunction

searchTerms: irregular heart rhythms including AV block

occasional.notes: Secondary to increased pulmonary blood flow

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating cardiac strain
Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia in cyanotic cases
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating partial atrioventricular septal defect and ventricular hypoplasia
Cardiac MRI for detailed ventricular morphology and function
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings

distinguishingFeatures: Complete AV septal defect involves a common AV valve rather than separate mitral and tricuspid valves
Usually presents with earlier and more severe heart failure
Severe hypoplasia of left-sided heart structures including aortic valve and ascending aorta
Absent or severely underdeveloped left ventricle
No atrial septal defect of the partial AVSD type

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Progressive congestive heart failure in neonate
Signs of low cardiac output including poor perfusion and metabolic acidosis
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th Edition. 2019.
Moller JH, et al. Congenital Heart Disease: A Clinical Guide. 2020.
